summary:
ASTRA – Astronaut Smart Health Monitoring System

ASTRA is an integrated health-monitoring platform designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions. It brings together astronauts, medical professionals, families, and Mission Control through dedicated interfaces. The platform monitors vital signs, tracks individual health patterns, and uses anomaly detection to identify unusual changes and generate smart alerts. It also provides an AI-powered health companion to help astronauts understand their health data and access general guidance, while enabling doctors to review health reports and provide recommendations. In addition, ASTRA supports offline data collection and local storage, allowing essential monitoring functions to continue when communication is unavailable, with synchronization once connectivity is restored. By combining continuous health monitoring, early anomaly detection, secure data sharing, and offline capabilities, ASTRA aims to improve astronauts' health awareness, support timely medical decisions, and contribute to safer and more sustainable human space exploration.
details:
Project Details – ASTRA

ASTRA is an integrated astronaut health-monitoring platform designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions by providing continuous health tracking, intelligent data analysis, and communication between astronauts, medical teams, families, and Mission Control.

How it works:

The system collects physiological data, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), and body temperature through connected sensors. The collected data is transmitted through an ESP32 microcontroller to the software platform, where it is processed, stored, and visualized through an interactive dashboard.

ASTRA analyzes health measurements in relation to each astronaut's personal baseline rather than relying only on general reference values. It identifies unusual changes, detects potential health risks, and generates smart alerts when attention may be needed.

The platform also includes:

- Health Dashboard: Displays real-time measurements, historical trends, and health summaries.

- Smart Alerts: Notifies astronauts and medical teams when unusual health patterns are detected.

- AI Health Assistant: Provides general, approved health guidance and helps astronauts understand their health information without replacing professional medical diagnosis.

- Medical Communication: Allows astronauts to share health updates and receive recommendations from medical professionals.

- Family Updates: Provides consent-based health summaries to help families stay informed.

- Mission Control Interface: Presents health reports and priority alerts to support mission decisions.

Technical Tools and Technologies:

The proposed software architecture uses:

- HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the user interface.

- Python and Flask for backend development and API communication.

- SQLite for data storage.

- Chart.js for health-data visualization.

- ESP32 as the microcontroller connecting hardware sensors to the software.

- Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or serial communication for data transmission, depending on the hardware setup.

The platform is designed with offline functionality in mind, allowing data to be stored locally and synchronized when communication becomes available again.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

ASTRA aims to improve astronaut health awareness, support early identification of potential health problems, reduce delays in medical communication, and provide medical teams with organized health information throughout space missions.

Beyond monitoring individual health measurements, the platform focuses on understanding changes over time and connecting different stakeholders through one integrated system.

Creativity and Design Considerations:

What makes ASTRA different is its integrated approach to astronaut healthcare. Instead of functioning as a simple monitoring application, it combines physiological monitoring, personalized health analysis, intelligent alerts, and communication into one platform.

Our team considered the unique challenges of space environments, including limited medical resources, communication delays, restricted access to healthcare professionals, data privacy, reliability, and the need for continuous monitoring during long-duration missions.

ASTRA aims to make healthcare more accessible, proactive, and connected, even when astronauts are millions of kilometers away from Earth.
